questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to travel to a German speaking country to better my knowledge of german and preferable not to a city that I had a prior connection to. Therefore, I chose to go to Munich.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Getting socially integrated to the university was very difficult. One thing was the language barrier making it difficult to get to know other students, but at the same time the university did not have a thorough introduction programm, which could have helped making the first couple of weeks less anxious.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The LMU has a very difficult and complex organisational structure, which leads to many bureaucratic processes being unintelligible. Especially since every institute/faculty has their own processes when it comes to applying for courses, finding information about the courses, exam structure, grading assessment etc. Luckily we had a very dedicated Erasmus-coordinator at my faculty, faculty 13, who was willing to go the distance in order to help us getting settled university wise.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: See my last answer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I dreaded the worst but ended up finding a room rather easily.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That commuting can take a lot of time, and that it is important to start your search for private housing as early as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult up front to understand what was demanded of you. It was necessary to email the receiving erasmus team.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to apply through their online portal and upload a certificate of sufficient language knowledge (Goethe test). The process was in itself not that difficult to figure out. My OLA was first signed as I was enrolled as a student.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A very helpful receiving team, who quickly answered any questions pr. mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up being enrolled in all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To no be afraid to contact the university if one has any questions regarding anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were made available for both BA and MA-students, but the requirements of the different exam projects (Prüfungleistungen) were differentiated. I.e. MA-students had to do more to receive the ECTS-points.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One did much less work in study groups. Most of the time Seminars functioned as a class discussion, Q&A-ish with the professor as the facilitator.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Kosmopo-Literatur
Autofiktion in der deutschsprachigen Gegenwartsliteratur
Zerbrechliche Welten - Heinrich von Kleists Dramen und Erzählungen
Unendliche Sehnsucht: Was heißt Romantik? 
Klasse, Familie, Nation - Herkunft erzählen 1970 und heute 
Søren Kierkegaard – Leben und Werk des Dichterphilosophen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can not say as courses are changed up each semester. I have heard that it is a poor idea to enroll in introductionary courses as they are much harder to pass compared to other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Inventory for the room.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing ended up being less expensive than expected. Usually students that end up renting private rooms pay a lot more in Munich than I did.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was for sure a lot of social and cultural clubs, which were available also for exchange students, but not much information was supplied. The sports club was impossible to get into because of the demand and the limited spots. Most of the time the ESN-network was the place to go if you wanted to join up on social activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, it is definitely a good idea to join ESN-organised events as they are great opportunities to meet a lot of different people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the nature around Munich to go for hikes/walks/jogs with people you meet. A great way to get to know people.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Rather easy. I did not find decisive differences between danish and German culture when it came to everyday life. The general culture of the university is quite different though.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not really mange to make a lot of local friends other than my roommates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is not so much a cultural difference as a societal one, but the bureaucratic processes in the beginning, fx applying to be a inhabitant of the city, was quite a hurdle and very confusing even with decent German proficiency. Other than that, supermarkets closing early and not being open on Sundays ended up actually being an obstacle when you had to structure your week.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general openeness of the Bavarians. Easy to do conversation with random people. And how normal it was to spend most of your time out and about in the city,

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Read up on what is demanded of you and be patient with the German bureaucracy .
Start searching for housing quickly.
Use the ESN-network if you feel lonely, especially in the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is always a good idea to introduce yourself to the professors and be on good terms with them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social and cultural aspect of getting to know people from all around the world, and especially from all around Europe. Also having the opportunity to travel around South-Germany. Being in contact with a university system that is so different to the one I was used to has also proven to be a quite educative experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Without a doubt participating on equal teams with German students, when the classes were conducted in German.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
